lines.vo: In 1940, Chevrolet sponsored a film about a robot butler.
His name: Roll-Oh. The film calls him "the chromium-plated butler."
One panel gives him his orders. Answer Door. Wash Dishes. Get Dinner. Make Bed.
Then the film admits it. Roll-Oh "is just a daydream after all."
His little brothers and sisters, it says, are "small mechanical servants that never ask for afternoons off."
A tea kettle that pulls out its own plug. An electric eye that turns on the lights.
And a motor car "simply full of robots."
Sixty-two years later, a robot finally came for the floors.
On September 18th, 2002, iRobot introduced the Roomba.
Its maker called it "the first automatic floor vac available in the U.S." Suggested price: one hundred ninety-nine dollars and ninety-five cents.
Roll-Oh or a Roomba: which one would you let in your house?
